claims.statement: Python package dependencies run systemone -> chess, while cli (via the langchain-chess[systemone] extra), apps/server and evals (both listing chess and systemone directly) depend on both chess and systemone; no workspace member depends on cli, server or evals.
libs/chess exposes an optional `systemone` extra that the CLI installs through (`langchain-chess[systemone]`), but langchain_chess source never imports langchain_chess_systemone.

create_chess_agent wraps each user middleware in the write guard, rejects two middlewares declaring the same own state key, and builds the stack ChessCore, then ForcedMoveMiddleware (if forced_move), then guarded extensions, then ChessSummarization when memory=True or a NoSummarization placeholder when fixed_topology=True, and finally StallRetry last, passing it to create_agent with tools=[] and ChessState.
create_chess_agent raises ChessContractError if the compiled graph's input schema exposes keys other than messages and position, or if two middlewares declare the same own state key.

A CallRecorder is attached as a callback to every chess agent graph so provider responses are captured for pricing, the graph is rejected if its input schema exposes keys other than messages and position, and model=None installs a NoModel that raises ChessContractError if called.

build_agent in libs/systemone turns a ChessContext into a chess agent for every surface, calling only the factories a policy needs: llm (chat model, NoSystemOne in System 1's slot under fixed_topology), systemone (no model so memory is off, SystemOneMiddleware with threshold and tournament_threshold forced to 0 and has_model=False) and hybrid (both); surface middleware runs after System 1.

The chess graph is registered in langgraph.json as apps/server graph.py:make_graph, with the FastAPI app from app.py as the HTTP app and .env as the env file; the image builds from the uv workspace (source.kind uv, package langchain-chess-server) and dockerfile_lines ADDs the pyproject.toml of libs/chess, libs/systemone, libs/cli and apps/server but not evals.

mise run test runs test:python (pytest -n auto with the 100% coverage gate) and test:web (`vp run -r test`); pytest excludes live and e2e markers by default (`-m not live and not e2e`), which run via mise run test:live (`-m live --no-cov`) and mise run test:e2e (builds the UI first).

mise run dev:web starts langgraph dev (default port 2024) and the web UI (default 5173 under /ui/), refuses to start if either port is in use, points the UI at the server via VITE_API_URL, prints the URLs once both respond, and stops all processes when either exits; ports are overridable with LANGGRAPH_PORT and WEB_PORT.
The web UI reaches the agent over HTTP using useStream on the chess graph, and apps/web, apps/review, evals/reports and packages/* form one pnpm workspace whose shared versions live in the catalog.
Server settings treat an environment key that is set but empty as a validation error rather than unset.
mise run test:uci plays two SemIf-only lcchess games against each other under fastchess and fails unless both games end with a result and no forfeit termination.

ServerSettings.typesafe() raises ValueError when TYPESAFE_API_KEY or TYPESAFE_BASE_URL is unset and is called only inside the server's pooled ranker factory, which build_agent invokes only for policies that run System 1, so only systemone and hybrid require those variables; ServerSettings also rejects a gateway or TypeSafe variable that is set but empty.
build_agent raises ChessContractError when memory is on for a model whose input limit is unknown.

make_graph returns shape() for runless calls (no execution runtime): a graph with no model, NoSystemOne and GameSetupMiddleware that needs no clients or credentials; only runs resolve a ChessContext and call build_graph (build_agent with fixed_topology=True, GameSetupMiddleware and a pooled ranker using a fresh ServerSettings), and both paths share the same topology.
GameSetupMiddleware writes the run's resolved ChessContext as a client-readable setup key only on the game's first turn, and never again.

Chat model construction (chat_model with output budget, profile and resolved model arguments) lives in langchain_chess.chat_models; the server builds its model with chat_model and the server-surface model arguments, while build_agent's default model uses the local surface.
Memory is a boolean setting (off by default) that keeps earlier turns summarized near the model's input limit; the README states that design decisions and measurements live in the OpenWiki.

ChessContext settings are versioned: VERSION is bumped on every schema change, DEFAULTS freezes each version's keys and defaults, MIGRATIONS carry one version to the next, migrate rejects unknown keys (or drops them) and newer versions, and resolve merges migrated sources over the defaults with later sources winning and an explicit null resetting a key.
The server resolves a run's settings from assistant context first and then config configurable, treating a source without a version as the current version and dropping keys the settings don't have.

mise run generate:settings runs langchain_chess_server.codegen to write ChessContext's JSON Schemas and TypeScript into packages/chess-ui/src/generated, and a test fails when the committed generated files are stale.

The evals workspace member (langchain-chess-evals, binary lcchess-evals) is never published and nothing imports it; mise tasks eval:positions:build, eval:positions:upload, eval:systemone and eval:systemone:baseline drive it, and it is included in the pytest, coverage, ruff and ty configuration.

StallRetry is always the last middleware in the core stack and retries only the provider call, once and without delay, on stream-stall errors (langchain-openai's StreamChunkTimeoutError); other errors still fail the turn and a stalled attempt records no call.
The CLI's uci and play commands build their agents with the shared build_agent from a ChessContext, optionally loaded from a settings file with load_file.
